title: VP defense struggling to find credible witnesses – prosecution
summary: As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte approaches its final stage, her defense team appears to be still struggling to get credible witnesses who can refute testimonies and…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol yesterday announced the names of the witnesses who will testify during whole-day hearings from Nov. 9 to 13.
Senate SMU / Joseph Vidal

MANILA, Philippines — As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte approaches its final stage, her defense team appears to be still struggling to get credible witnesses who can refute testimonies and documentary evidence presented by prosecutors, a spokesman for the House prosecution team said yesterday.

“They presented a supposedly expert witness, but his testimony was very far off from the Article of Impeachment that he had to rebut. Because if they really wanted to prove the VP’s innocence, they should have done that at the earliest by presenting their first witness,” Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said at a news briefing.

He said it was evident that defense lawyers were unable to present witnesses who could directly shed light on the P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth of the Vice President and her spouse Manases Carpio.

“It speaks about how difficult it is for the defense really to look for witnesses that are competent, credible to provide documents before the court that will prove the innocence of the Vice President,” Adiong said.
His remarks came after the Senate impeachment court’s cancellation of the Nov. 26 and 27 hearings due to unavailability of defense witnesses.

The Lanao del Sur lawmaker said the primary issue was not whether the defense lawyers were being treated fairly, but whether they were prepared to present witnesses capable of explaining the evidence against Duterte.

“It’s about how prepared they are and how capable are they to really provide or present witnesses that can actually answer all these questions. And it’s really difficult for them,” Adiong, chairman of the House committee on suffrage and electoral reforms, pointed out.
It was forensic accounting expert Alexander Cabrera who earlier identified the P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth amassed by the Duterte couple from 2022 to 2025.
“The witnesses whom they decided to sit on the witness stand, they haven’t proven anything yet that could establish the VP’s innocence – even a single document,” he said.
He pointed out that the prosecution’s allegations were fully documented and supported by bank records, corporate filings, tax documents and Duterte’s statements of assets, liabilities and net worth.

Adiong and prosecution adviser and former congressman Robert Ace Barbers also said the Duterte camp may still rebut the withdrawn grave threat charges against the Vice President – but this time before the courts.
“They (defense lawyers) still have a venue. It’s not because the grave threats charges have been withdrawn in the Senate impeachment trial means they can no longer refute the charges,” Barbers said.
“So I really find it irrelevant to say that there is no more venue to answer these allegations in this article,” he maintained, adding the case is now with the Quezon City regional trial court.
Barbers was reacting to Duterte’s complaint about supposedly losing an opportunity to present evidence of alleged threats made by police personnel against her.

The grave threats against Duterte stemmed from her announcement at her online press briefing in November 2024 that she had contracted an assassin to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez.

In a statement last Saturday, Duterte claimed she had in her possession at least five documented threats allegedly made by police personnel against her, the Office of the Vice President and her family.
She blamed the prosecution’s withdrawal of the grave threats article for what she claimed was her lost opportunity to present the evidence at her Senate trial.
Barbers stressed the withdrawal did not end the separate criminal case against Duterte.

Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., meanwhile, has challenged Duterte to submit evidence supporting her allegations of police misconduct involving her former household staff member and four other people, saying such claims should be properly investigated.
He urged Duterte and her office to submit documents and other evidence that could help investigators establish what really happened. — Mark Ernest Villeza
